description: Make Apple Reminders a trustworthy bidirectional intake: propagate deliberate Apple-side deletion to the linked canonical Markdown task, normalize new reminders from six synced lists, keep Repeat Apple-only, safely automate high-confidence intake cleanup, and verify the ten-minute macOS bridge is installed and healthy.

decisions.canonicalTaskStore: A linked Apple Reminder may create, update, complete, reopen, move, or deliberately delete its canonical Markdown task. Unlinked Markdown tasks remain untouched by Apple-side deletion.
decisions.routing: The selected list is authoritative for Work, Personal, House, and Waiting. New Inbox and Quick Wins items are locally routed only when confidence is high; ties remain Inbox with #needs-triage.
decisions.cleanup: Deterministic cleanup runs automatically. When a configured provider passes LaunchAgent preflight, it may reword only after agreeing with the local high-confidence route and returning a concise valid action.
decisions.safety: A missing Reminder becomes a deletion signal only after a successful authoritative read of its configured list. Permission failures, unavailable lists, and partial reads must fail closed and never delete Markdown tasks.
decisions.privateState: Reminder IDs, tombstones, audit history, list IDs, Mac paths, and model credentials remain local and ignored. The public repository contains no personal task content or runtime state.

userStories.title: Configure the six-list Reminders workflow
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want Inbox, Quick Wins, Waiting, Work, Personal, and House to be explicit synced Apple Reminders sources while Repeat remains Apple-only.
acceptanceCriteria: Expose configurable names and private IDs for Inbox, Quick Wins, Waiting, Work, Personal, and House; migrate existing Work, Personal, House, Waiting, and Inbox settings without overwriting user changes.
Read and import only the configured lists. A reminder in an unconfigured Apple list is ignored and produces no task, move, or deletion.

Map the selected list to canonical metadata: Inbox -> #needs-triage, Quick Wins -> #quick-win and #10min, Waiting -> #blocked and #follow-up, Work -> #work, Personal -> #personal, and House -> #house. Repeat is not read for projection or native tags.
Keep list identifiers, settings, and per-item links in ignored local state; public defaults contain names only and no account identifiers.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Repeat is read only as a safety boundary so a linked item moved there is not mistaken for deletion; it is never imported, edited, tagged, or deletion-reconciled.

userStories.title: Propagate confirmed Apple-side deletion to Markdown
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want deleting a linked incomplete Reminder in Apple Reminders to remove its linked canonical Markdown task so that the two systems do not resurrect work I intentionally deleted.
acceptanceCriteria: Treat a missing linked Reminder as a deletion only after its configured list was read successfully and the exact linked ID is absent; permission errors, an unavailable list, an empty partial response, and a sync failure cannot cause deletion.
Remove only the exact linked task checkbox and bridge-owned Details line from the configured Task Inbox. Preserve unrelated Markdown, manually authored child notes, and unlinked tasks.

Record a private deletion tombstone with Reminder ID, task ID, timestamp, list, and source so the next sync does not recreate either side; support an explicit restore action from the private activity view.

Deleting a parent follows an explicit hierarchy rule: delete linked descendants only when they were mirrored from that Apple parent; otherwise hold the parent for review rather than deleting user-authored children.
Dry-run reports proposed deletions without writing; live deletion is idempotent and is recorded in sync activity without exposing private IDs in the UI.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Deletion is intentionally distinct from completion. Completing a Reminder continues to mark the linked Markdown task complete.

userStories.title: Import and normalize newly created Apple Reminders
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want a new Reminder in one of my configured lists to become one understandable, linked Markdown task without duplicate reminders or invented task data.
acceptanceCriteria: Import every previously unlinked Reminder from a configured list once, assign a stable task/reminder link, and preserve title, notes, due date, priority, completion, flag, URL, and supported recurrence data.
Run deterministic cleanup: remove transport syntax, duplicate tags, Obsidian block IDs, formatting artifacts, and redundant whitespace; place substantive Reminder notes in a Details line.
Do not invent a due date when Apple supplied none. Apply only configured default tags such as duration and status, with clear source attribution in the private activity record.
Write the normalized title, canonical tags, and configured list back to the linked Reminder only after successful import; then invoke the native-tag Shortcut after the bridge succeeds.
Use list selection as the default route. High-confidence Inbox and Quick Wins items may move automatically; ambiguous input remains in Inbox with #needs-triage rather than silently moving it.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The cleanup pass must not change a task's meaning, delete user notes, or copy private Reminder IDs into Markdown.

userStories.title: Provide clear, reviewable task rewording and routing
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want unclear new tasks improved into concise, actionable wording and routed appropriately without an opaque model silently changing commitments.
acceptanceCriteria: Generate an explainable cleanup/reword proposal that distinguishes deterministic formatting changes from semantic wording changes.
Use local rules first. Optional model assistance is off until explicitly configured, uses the existing provider privacy disclosure, and sends only the task fields required for the proposal.
Allow approve, edit, reject, and defer actions. Approval may update the linked Markdown task and its Reminder title/list/tags in the same reconciliation cycle.

High-confidence local routes may move automatically. Semantic rewording is automatic only when the configured model agrees with the local route and returns a valid concise action; unavailable or disagreeing models leave deterministic wording unchanged.
Keep the original incoming wording in private activity history long enough to explain a proposal, never in public source or public logs.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: No model call occurs without provider preflight. Local cleanup and routing remain safe fallbacks.

userStories.title: Reconcile moves, tags, and repeat behavior without conflicts
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want list changes, tags, flags, completion, and recurrence to stay consistent across Apple Reminders and Obsidian after intake or review.
acceptanceCriteria: Treat direct list moves as category changes and update corresponding canonical tags; preserve explicit user tags unless they contradict the selected list's managed category.
Make the native-tag Shortcut run only after the bridge succeeds and report missing Shortcut, permission, or tag failures as stale/failed integration status without discarding task changes.
Apply a documented field-level conflict policy, record conflicts privately, and never delete or overwrite a task solely because a concurrent reconciliation is ambiguous.
Prevent duplicate imports, duplicate status/duration tags, and endless list/tag oscillation across two or more sync runs.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Native Apple tags remain a projection. Markdown plus private link state remain the cross-system identity source.

userStories.title: Install and verify the ten-minute macOS bridge
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want the Reminders bridge installed, active, and observable on my Mac so that two-way changes are processed every ten minutes even while Obsidian is closed.
acceptanceCriteria: After implementation verification, run the explicit installer against the intended vault and install or upgrade only Uptick-owned companion files and the com.uptick.reminders-sync user LaunchAgent.
Verify launchctl shows the agent bootstrapped for the current GUI user, its plist has a 600-second StartInterval and RunAtLoad, and kickstart completes without error.

Verify remindctl authorization, the six configured lists, Repeat exclusion, the installed native-tag Shortcut name, writable local log/state paths, and a successful dry-run before enabling normal sync.
Run one controlled live reconciliation with a non-sensitive fixture or approved test item, then verify the activity record and log show bridge success followed by native-tag processing.
Surface fresh, stale, disabled, and failed status in Uptick; document safe repair, upgrade, and uninstall behavior without deleting user tasks, reminders, state, or the Shortcut.
Typecheck passes
fixtureCoverage: failed bridge does not run Shortcut
userStories.notes: Installation and macOS permissions are action-time owner-approved steps. Do not install a scheduler while only writing or reviewing this PRD.

userStories.title: Document and test the bidirectional contract
userStories.description: As an Uptick user, I want clear documentation and regression coverage so I know exactly what creating, moving, completing, deleting, rewording, and scheduling do.
acceptanceCriteria: Update the README and guided walkthrough with the six-list table, deletion behavior, cleanup/reword automation boundary, list authority, Repeat exclusion, and 10-minute LaunchAgent verification steps.
Add end-to-end fixtures for create, edit, move, complete, delete, tombstone, restore, conflict, disabled module, unavailable list, stale integration, and absent native Shortcut states.
Run Reminders, workflow-assistant, renderer, structure, clean-install, public-release-boundary, release-audit, Python syntax, JavaScript syntax, and macOS smoke checks.
Confirm no private task text, list IDs, account values, local vault paths, or live state enter tracked files, tests, release assets, or public logs.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Release packaging remains limited to documented public plugin assets; macOS helpers remain source-tree companions.
